sentences.text: He further submits that looking to the age of the injured, 40% of income should have been added in the head of future prospects.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the accident appellant / injured has suffered grievous injuries and fracture in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8987 2 MA-1953-2020 right leg.
He further submits that permanent disability should also have been considered at least 7.5% looking to the permanent disability of 15% which has been proved by Dr. NK Gupta (AW-3).
He further submits that a meager amount has been awarded in the head of transport, attendance which should be enhanced to Rs.5,000/- in each head.
On these submissions, he prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.

sentences.text:
4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.
From perusal of the record, it reveals that in the accident the appellant has suffered grievous injuries and fracture in the right leg also.

Permanent disability has been given to 15% and Dr. N.K.
Gupta (AW-3) has also proved the disability certificate, therefore, keeping in view the evidence available in this regard, this Court is of the view that 7.5% permanent disability is assessed.
In light of the aforesaid, where the income of the injured is taken on guess work, Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.

Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8987 3 MA-1953-2020 27.03.2017 income of the appellant/injured is to be taken as Rs.6,950/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour' and for this judgment passed by the Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198 shall be referred.

entities.text: Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Appellant / injured was 37 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi's case (Supra), 40% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects.
The amount awarded in the head of transport and attendance is also on lower side, therefore, Rs.5,000/- is awarded in each head.

6. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.1,31,355/-
Permanent Disability:
(Rs.6950/- + 40% FP x 7.5% PD x 15 x 12)
For loss of income Rs.4000/-
For medical expenses Rs.2,16,337/-
For pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-

For attendance Rs.5000/-
 For transport Rs.5000/-
For special diet Rs.10,000/-

Total: Rs.3,96,692/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.2,60,337/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.1,36,355/-
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.3,96,692/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.2,60,337/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.1,36,355/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / injured is allowed to the extent as indicated herein-above.
Other terms and conditions of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8987 4 MA-1953-2020 impugned award including rate of interest shall remain intact.

The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate as awarded by learned Claims Tribunal in Om Prakash Patidar vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. ... on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184727876/
